samples.summary: Design doc not updated for the new container-scoped indent/outdent rule
samples.evidence: notes.md's "List controls and interactive checkboxes — shipped (issue #754)" section is the canonical record of this behaviour and is quite precise about it: "Every command applies to all lines the selection covers, blank lines excepted" (l.785-786) and "the neighbour walks (`itemAbove` / `parentOf`) stop at a change of quote depth" (l.796-799). This delta adds a rule the doc does not state: `shift()` now moves only the selected lines whose quote depth matches the *top* list line's, silently leaving other-container lines in place (list-commands.ts:323-334), and it redefines "same container" as a count of `>` characters rather than prefix-text equality so `>` and `> ` are the same blockquote (list-commands.ts:143-145). CONTRIBUTING.md:58-60 asks for the existing doc to be updated rather than left behind. Cost is confined to doc accuracy — the code behaves as intended.

samples.summary: Second, divergent blockquote-prefix parser in the same package
samples.evidence: `commands.ts:278` uses `QUOTE_RE = /^\s*>\s?/` for the Quote toggle while `list-commands.ts:45` uses `/^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` and now layers a `quoteDepth()` notion of container identity on top of it. Two parsers of the same markdown construct in one package will answer differently for nested (`> > `) or deeply indented quotes; this delta deepens the divergence by giving one of them semantics (container identity) the other has no equivalent of. A shared quote-prefix helper would be the reuse point. No user-visible cost today.
